articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the April 1991 issue of "SJAA Ephemeris," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It is identified as Volume 3, Number 4 of the newsletter.

articles.title: FACE ON MARS IS TRYING TO TALK
articles.summary: The article sensationally claims that the "Face on Mars" is attempting to communicate, with its lips observed moving in photographs taken by the Soviet Mars 23 orbiter. Scientists like Dr. Peter Bosch suggest the mile-long monument could be an intelligent robot or a life form, leading a Soviet team of photo analysts and lip-readers to decipher its message, which has reportedly been interpreted as "Come to the SJAA auction." This intriguing development has prompted calls from some scientists for a manned mission to Mars for direct investigation.

articles.title: APRIL STARRY NIGHTS
articles.summary: Richard Stanton's "APRIL STARRY NIGHTS" introduces a discussion for the month, starting with a personal reflection on current "Headline News" that he finds believable. He evokes a sense of wonder and connection by referencing the longstanding "call of Mars," hinting at a focus on celestial events or astronomical topics for the current period.

articles.title: APRIL 6TH THE SEARCH FOR EXTRA-TERRESTRIAL LIFE
articles.summary: This document outlines a series of astronomy-related events for April and early May, including a general meeting on April 6th featuring a talk on the search for extraterrestrial life. Other key events include multiple public star parties, an Introductory Observational Astronomy class, and an Astronomy Day celebration. The schedule also notes board meetings, a daylight saving time change, and a May auction.

articles.title: SJAA HOTLINE
articles.summary: The SJAA Hotline features a humorous, satirical announcement claiming that 'The Face on Mars' has divulged a message for people to attend the SJAA auction. This fabricated revelation, reportedly from 'dubitable scientists' at a 'Mars conference,' is clearly presented as an April Fool's joke, with confirmation pending an investigation by 'the Great April Fool.' It serves as an entertaining, non-serious promotion for an event.

articles.title: CALENDAR NOTES
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) will host Dr. Peter Backus from NASA on April 6th for their General Meeting to discuss the Search for Extra-terrestrial Life, with a Board meeting preceding it. Additionally, volunteers are sought for Astronomy Day on April 20th at Branham Lane Park, where solar observations and evening sky viewing will take place, and members are encouraged to promote the event.

articles.title: SJAA OFFICERS SELECTED
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) re-elected its current officers at the March 3 Board Meeting, who were subsequently installed at the General Meeting. Tom Ahl will continue as President, Paul Mancuso as Vice-President, Jack Peterson as Treasurer, and Jim Van Nuland as Secretary. The article also clarified the four board members whose terms are continuing for another year: Wolfgang Hanisch, Gene Cisneros, Del Johnson, and Jack Peterson.

articles.title: SCHOOLHOUSE STAR PARTIES
articles.summary: The SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association) recently held a star party in Hayward on February 20th, acknowledging the volunteers who traveled there. The article makes a strong call for more volunteers, particularly from members living in 'outer limits' like Hayward and south of San Jose, to help with future school star parties. It emphasizes that volunteering is easy, rewarding, and beneficial for both the community and the club.

articles.title: AUCTION XI
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association is hosting its 11th Annual Bay-Area Astronomical Swap Meet and Auction on May 4. This year, the event will take place at a new location, the Community Room in the Milpitas library, due to construction issues at the previously used Red Cross building.

articles.title: JOB OFFER
articles.summary: Minolta Planetarium is seeking a part-time Planetarium Operator with a background in space science or astronomy. The role involves operating equipment and running public programs during evenings and weekends. Interested candidates should send their resume to Caron Silnick at DeAnza College in Cupertino, CA.

articles.title: THE ASTRONOMERS
articles.summary: A new six-part PBS series titled "THE ASTRONOMERS", narrated by Richard Chamberlain, is set to explore groundbreaking astronomical discoveries such as black holes, quasars, dark matter, gravity waves, and exoplanets. The series aims to provide an exciting approach to science programming by focusing on both the universe's mysteries and the lives of the astronomers making these discoveries.

articles.title: MOON STRUCK
articles.summary: The document presents two main topics: an amateur astronomer's query and a television series announcement. Bill Dellinges asks for help calculating how many years it would take for every day of the year to experience a full moon, detailing his partial, manual effort that suggested an 85-year period for selected months. Additionally, it announces "THE ASTRONOMERS," a six-episode PBS series airing on KTEH, Channel 54, which explores major astronomical questions and discoveries, covering topics from dark matter and quasars to the Big Bang, gravity waves, star life cycles, and exoplanet detection.

articles.title: WORKING WITH CHANNEL 54 - KTEH
articles.summary: KTEH, a PBS station, is holding its annual auction in the fourth week of April, interrupting a new 6-part series. The author is seeking volunteers from SJAA to assist with the auction on April 22nd to enhance community presence, with shifts from 5-6 PM to midnight including food, and has also requested KTEH announce SJAA's Hot Line number during "THE ASTRONOMERS" showings.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: The "COMET COMMENTS" article by Don Machholz details recent comet activity, including an outburst from Halley's Comet and Carolyn Shoemaker's 22nd comet discovery (1991f), making her second in named comet finds. It also provides information on new comets Shoemaker-Levy (1991e), Periodic Comet Shoemaker-Levy (1991f), and McNaught-Russell (1991g), including their discovery dates and preliminary orbital characteristics. Shoemaker's discoveries are noted for being faint and part of a program to identify Earth-crossing objects.

articles.title: COMET EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document provides ephemeris data for two comets, Comet Levy (1990c) and Comet Metcalf-Brewington (1991a), covering the period from March 30 to May 4. For each comet, it lists daily Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (DEC) for both 1950 and 2000 epochs, along with elongation, sky visibility, and estimated visual magnitude to aid observers.

articles.title: THIS MONTH'S METEORS
articles.summary: This document provides a guide to meteor showers active during the month, detailing their dates, peak rates, radiant points, and other characteristics, with a focus on the April Lyrids. It also includes updates on two periodic comets, Takamizawa (1990h) and Kowal (1990i), reporting their recent recovery, orbital information, and predicted brightness.

articles.title: OBSERVING PLANETS IN THE DAYTIME
articles.summary: This article provides practical advice for observing planets during the daytime, offering a partial solution for those seeking more viewing opportunities. It details methods for locating brighter planets like Venus (often visible naked-eye once sighted), Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn using both equatorial and altazimuth telescopes. Techniques include using setting circles with an equatorially mounted scope and a "star drifting" method for altazimuth mounts, enabling successful daytime astronomical observation.

articles.title: METEOR NOTES
articles.summary: As spring arrives, meteor observers return, though sporadic meteor rates are at their lowest. However, minor showers in the Virgo-Leo area and notably the annual April Lyrids will increase viewing opportunities. The April Lyrids are predicted to peak on April 22nd around 1200 PST, with the best observing conditions in the early morning hours of that day, offering swift, white-to-yellow meteors despite potentially lower local rates.

articles.title: INDIVIDUAL SHOWER NOTES
articles.summary: This document provides notes on individual meteor showers, detailing their characteristics and historical activity. It mentions the Virginids, Sigma Leonids, and Mu Virginids as components of Hoffmeister's visual Virginids and the Scorpius-Sagittarius system. The April Lyrids are described as a currently weak annual shower, contrasting with stronger historical displays recorded in 1884, 1922, and 1948.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: This document, titled "ASTRO ADS," serves as a free classifieds section for non-commercial advertisers selling astronomically related products or services. It features numerous listings for used telescopes (e.g., Celestron C8, Dobsonian, Meade Comet Tracker, Questar), eyepieces, filters, mounts, finderscopes, and related accessories. Ads are accepted monthly and run for approximately three months.

articles.title: AUCTION XI
articles.summary: The eleventh annual Bay Area Astronomical Auction is scheduled for May 4, inviting participants to sell or donate astronomical and telescope-making items. The article details the pre-registration process, including item listing, minimum bids, and a 10% sales commission (or outright donation), with proceeds benefiting public astronomy education. In addition to the main auction, a Swap Meet and a Silent Auction for larger items will also be held.

articles.title: DIRECTIONS TO THE MILPITAS LIBRARY
articles.summary: This document provides directions to the Milpitas Library via highways 17/880 and 237, including specific turns onto Milpitas Blvd. It also details an event featuring a Swap Meet from 2 PM to 5 PM, an auction starting at 6 PM, and requests a $1 donation for auction registration. Refreshments will be available.

articles.title: SJAA AUCTION PRE-REGISTRATION
articles.summary: This document is a pre-registration form for an auction organized by SJAA. It allows participants to list items for donation or sale, including quantity, minimum bid, and a brief description, along with personal contact information.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP APPLICATION
articles.summary: This document outlines the membership application process for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) and introduces their monthly publication, "EPHEMERIS." Members are encouraged to submit typed articles for publication to editor John P. Gleason by the 12th of the previous month.

articles.title: Membership only: $10 Membership/S&T: $28 Junior (under 18): $18
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It outlines various membership tiers—standard, with Sky & Telescope magazine, and junior—along with their respective annual fees of $10, $28, and $18. The form provides instructions for submission, including the treasurer's mailing address and details for payment via check.
